A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WildCAT3D work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original WildCAT3D benchmark scores, ablations, appearance-embedding analysis and qualitative reconstruction results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative Gaussian Splatting renderings and depth-error examples.

M1.justification: WildCAT3D’s appearance encoder, guidance mechanism, warp conditioning and training/inference procedures are unchanged. The projection-layer explanation added to Section 3.4 already appeared in v1 Appendix B.4. Gaussian Splatting is added as a downstream evaluation, without modifying WildCAT3D.

E1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the reported appearance-retrieval image source from MegaDepth to approximately 10K MegaScenes images. The main training datasets and DTU, Mip-NeRF 360, Re10K and MegaScenes benchmark coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the released and MegaScenes-trained Zero-1-to-3 and ZeroNVS variants, SD-Inpaint and MS NVS. The ablation comparator sets also remain unchanged. Gaussian Splatting is used downstream, not evaluated as a competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix A.4 extends reconstruction evaluation by initializing a Gaussian Splatting representation from VGGSfM geometry and rendering novel views and depth maps. Existing benchmark resolutions, view grouping, training budgets and the 15K-image MegaScenes metric subset are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.5 and Figure 11 examine depth-error propagation through two qualitative failure cases. Appendix A.4 also extends the reconstruction analysis with Gaussian Splatting outputs. Existing component ablations, MegaScenes-only training analysis and embedding clustering are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 10 adds Gaussian Splatting views and depth maps, and Figure 11 adds qualitative depth-failure results. All 260 numerical entries in Tables 1–3 match after accounting for rounding and the explicitly stated tenfold KID display scaling; no numerical performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: The conditional-probability formulations, appearance assumptions and Plücker-ray construction are retained. The added design explanations introduce no new mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 qualifies the data-use framing by emphasizing fewer curated sources while exploiting more unfiltered samples. Its conclusion explicitly describes the experiments as limited in scale and foundational for web-scale NVS. The three principal contributions and state-of-the-art claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning flickering, saturation changes, depth-error propagation, coarse retrieval-based text control and greater training cost than MS NVS. Section 3.2 also explains the advantages of deriving appearance from images rather than textual metadata.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the approximate retrieval-bank size, MegaScenes and CO3D dataset sizes, Gaussian Splatting initialization, and MS NVS hardware/training-time context. WildCAT3D’s previously documented architecture, hardware and training schedule remain unchanged; the added dataset counts do not establish expanded training.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kerbl et al. (2023) for Gaussian Splatting and explicitly discusses the computational tradeoff relative to MS NVS. The existing related-work section and its principal positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose are retained. Changes comprise localized explanatory paragraphs, expanded limitations and implementation discussion, new Appendix A.5, wording corrections, and replacement of the preprint footer with the NeurIPS 2025 conference designation.

P2.justification: v2 extends Figure 10, adds Figure 11, and adjusts figure/table placement. Tables 1–3 use reduced numerical precision and labeled KID scaling with explanatory captions. Existing figure images and overall table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the paper easier to assess through concrete depth-failure examples, expanded reconstruction evidence, clearer limitations and explicit computational tradeoffs. These improve supporting evidence and transparency, while the core method and quantitative benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
